subject: OKR gap analysis & cross-team commitments ahead of QBR
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: OKR gap analysis & cross-team commitments ahead of QBR

Team —

I ran a quick gap analysis against our Q2 OKRs and attached a matrix showing where we are vs. plan (see attachment: okr_gap_matrix.csv). High level: two KRs are off-track in a way that will materially affect our QBR narrative unless we either (a) re-scope the KR to reflect realistic deliverables or (b) secure cross-team commitments that remove blockers by the end of the month.

Key items:
- KR-SRV-1 (Reduce avg latency 95p by 20%): currently at +8% vs. target; root cause is sustained telemetry showing cache misses and a spike in cold-starts for long-tail requests. Needs infra prioritization (Vivek).
- KR-ENG-3 (Integrations: ship 3 marketplace connectors): one connector is blocked by a vendor API change; Marissa can negotiate an ETA with the partner.
- KR-DEV-2 (Eval regression rate <3%): slipping after last model swap; requires an eval run and rollback plan from Product (Laura/Tessa).

Proposal (options for QBR framing):
1) Conservative: re-scope KR-ENG-3 to 2 connectors for committed scope; mark the third as stretch and note dependency on VendorX.
2) Aggressive: keep scope and request dedicated infra burst + a team of 1 SWE from platform for 3 weeks to unblock latency work.

Immediate asks (please respond with owner + firm ETA by EOD today):
- Vivek: can infra commit to a prioritized capacity bump and short-term kernel work to address cache cold starts? If yes, provide target date and ticket/SOW id.
- Marissa: confirm if we can push connector #3 to next quarter and whether we should proactively tell Acme (Sarah Liu) now.
- Laura/Tessa: can you produce a one-slide rollback plan + results from one eval run by next Tue (2026-06-23)?

I've also attached a short QBR prep memo (qbr_prep_memo.md) with suggested deck bullets. We'll finalize the QBR narrative tomorrow morning and pull the owner list into the deck.

Thanks — please be decisive on owners so I can lock the deck.

— Dylan
Dylan Brooks
VP, Serving & Platform
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: okr_gap_matrix.csv (text/csv)]
[Attachment: qbr_prep_memo.md (text/markdown)]

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 10:01:00 -0700
Subject: Re: OKR gap analysis & cross-team commitments ahead of QBR

Dylan —

Thanks for the matrix and clear asks. Quick clarifications:
- For the rollback plan we need the exact eval job parameters (model version, dataset slice). Tessa, can you paste the eval config?
- On procurement/legal: if we need a short-term dedicated capacity bump that crosses committed spend, Legal will want an estimated delta. Marissa, any estimate on impact to cost if we take the aggressive option?

I'll prepare a one-slide rollback framework; will mark owners for the actions I can take.

Laura
Laura Bennett
Head of Product
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 11:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: OKR gap analysis & cross-team commitments ahead of QBR

Looping Sarah for visibility on the connector status. Sarah — vendor changed their auth flow last week which impacted the marketplace connector we were building for you. I have a proposed approach: delay connector #3 to next quarter and prioritize the two other connectors so we can hit the customer-facing milestones.

To Dylan/Laura: I recommend we adopt the Conservative option for the QBR narrative (call the third connector a stretch). That avoids asking for extra infra spend this week and gives us room to renegotiate with VendorX. I'm attaching a short scope doc with the suggested wording for the QBR slide.

Costs: delaying connector #3 saves ~0.6 FTE equivalent of engineering time this quarter; if we go Aggressive (infra + 1 SWE), estimate incremental spend ~ $28k (short-term capacity + contract for one SWE).

— Marissa
Senior Director, Growth
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: ProposedScope_v2.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)]

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: OKR gap analysis & cross-team commitments ahead of QBR

Dylan / team —

We can prioritize the cache/cold-start work but need a formal request in our infra queue (I created a stub ticket: infra-6571). ETA for a targeted capacity bump and kernel tweaks: 2026-06-25 EOD, assuming we get aligned on expected peak QPS and sign-off on the change window. I'll need the following from Product:
- expected 95p QPS for the affected endpoints (estimate by EOD today)
- approval for a 2-hour change window during low traffic next week

If you want the aggressive path sooner than 06/25, we can buy burst capacity from VendorX; Procurement will need a PO and Procurement contact (procurement@vendorx.com). I've attached the infra ticket stub.

— Vivek
VP, Infrastructure
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: infra_capacity_request.ticket (text/plain)]

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Jun 2026 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: OKR gap analysis & cross-team commitments ahead of QBR

Good cadence — thanks for the quick replies. Final decisions for the deck:
- Narrative: use the Conservative option; call connector #3 a stretch and flag VendorX dependency. Marissa to notify Acme (Sarah) by EOD today (owner: marissa_cole).
- Infra: Vivek to proceed with infra-6571 and target 2026-06-25 EOD for the capacity bump (owner: vivek_kulkarni). Please convert infra-6571 into a signed SOW or ticket with Procurement looped (procurement@vendorx.com).
- Eval/rollback: Laura/Tessa produce one-slide rollback + eval results by 2026-06-23 (owner: laura_bennett, tessa_morgan).

Action list (add to QBR deck and mark completion column):
- Marissa: send customer comms to Sarah (Acme) — due 2026-06-18 EOD.
- Vivek: infra ticket -> capacity bump -> update deck with ETA — due 2026-06-25.
- Laura/Tessa: rollback slide + eval results — due 2026-06-23.
- Dylan: finalize QBR narrative & deck bullets — due 2026-06-20 morning.

I've added the QBR deck link here: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/QBR-Deck-2026Q2 — please drop your one-slide artifacts into the folder under /inputs. I'll lock the deck on 2026-06-20 at 10:00am PT. If anyone needs an exception to the timeline, call it out now.

— Dylan
VP, Serving & Platform
Redwood Inference
[Link: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/QBR-Deck-2026Q2]
